title: Short: 100 MBBS seats from next session: Itoo

 Jammu and Kashmir Health Minister Sakeena Itoo announced that AIIMS Awantipora is set to offer 100 MBBS seats starting from the next academic session, significantly enhancing medical education opportunities in the region
 Powered by
 Read Full Story 
 This development will allow more medical aspirants from Jammu and Kashmir to pursue their studies within the Union Territory, reducing the need to seek education elsewhere
 Powered by
 Read Full Story 
 The operationalisation of AIIMS Awantipora is expected to improve access to specialized healthcare and advanced medical facilities, particularly benefiting patients from south Kashmir
 Powered by
 Read Full Story 
 Union Health Minister J P Nadda emphasized the importance of making the institute functional as soon as possible, with support from Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, who has visited the site multiple times
 Powered by
 Read Full Story 
 The new AIIMS institute aims to strengthen patient care and lessen the necessity for residents to travel outside the region for specialized treatments
 Powered by
 Read Full Story 
 During a review meeting, Minister Itoo also addressed the tragic death of Adnan Ahmed Rather, a final-year MBBS student from Sopore, whose body was found in Bangladesh
 Powered by
 Read Full Story 
 Itoo requested Nadda's help in ensuring the swift return of the student's mortal remains to his family, who are undergoing significant distress due to the incident
 Powered by
 Read Full Story 
 Nadda assured that he would communicate with the concerned ministry to facilitate the return of Adnan Ahmed Rather's remains, offering all possible assistance to the grieving family
